title: Tool execution spiral: halting guarantees and safe result injection
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Multi-tool chains (chat->search->code-exec->formatter) sometimes create runaway execution loops when tool outputs are reinjected into the prompt or when tool chains call functions recursively. Current mitigations (max depth counters and simple timeouts) are brittle and cause false positives or allow pathological loops. This ticket introduces a combined approach: deterministic halting heuristics, safe result-injection contracts, and compatibility shims for legacy function-calling styles so we can enable richer streaming + tool workflows without increasing customer risk. The goal is to provide runtime guarantees that a single request cannot loop indefinitely and to ensure tool results injected back into the model are sanitized and annotated so downstream tools and the model can reason about provenance and stop conditions.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic recursion detector is implemented that flags cyclic tool-invocation graphs with > N re-entrancies within a single request and halts further tool calls with a clear structured error
Result injection must include a provenance header in structured output when reinjecting into the model (tool_id, call_id, depth, truncated_flag)
Streaming responses preserve tool-call boundaries and expose safe cancellation hooks to the client and runtime
Compatibility layer accepts legacy function-calling payloads (v1) and maps them to the new structured contract with no loss of fidelity in >95% of recorded integrations

End-to-end integration tests covering chained tool scenarios (including search->summarize->tool-run) show no false-positive halts on normal workloads and correctly stop pathological recursions introduced by test harnesses
Telemetry surfaces five new metrics and alert thresholds (recursive_call_rate, injected_result_truncations, tool_chain_depth_p95, chain_halts_per_1k, streaming_cancellation_rate)
design_decisions: Use a hybrid static/dynamic approach: static graph invariants for known tool dependencies plus dynamic per-request reentrancy counters
Enforce a small, fixed upper bound on tool-chain depth (configurable per-tenant) and a separate soft bound that triggers best-effort summarization instead of halting
Result injection will use an explicit structured wrapper (content + metadata) instead of free-text injection to enable downstream tooling and provenance checks
Compatibility shim will normalize legacy function-calling payloads into the structured wrapper at the API ingress boundary, delegating validation to the runtime
Streaming will emit boundary markers for tool call start/end and support mid-stream safe cancellation to avoid partial tool restarts
technical_design:
Runtime components: 1) Invocation Guard: attaches a request-scoped invocation context that tracks (tool_id, call_id, parent_call_id, depth, timestamp). 2) Reentrancy Detector: maintains a small LRU of recent call signatures (hash(tool_id + normalized_args + reprompt_signature)) to detect cycles with adjustable sensitivity. 3) Safe Injector: when a tool returns content intended for model reinjection, the injector wraps it in structured JSON: {"tool_id":...,"call_id":...,"depth":...,"truncated":...,"payload":...}. The injector also runs lightweight sanitizers (strip long repeating tokens, remove dangerous shell fragments for code-exec tools, redact PII if KMS policy indicates) before reinjection. 4) Streaming Adapter: augments token stream with boundary events (EVENT:TOOL_START, EVENT:TOOL_RESULT, EVENT:TOOL_END) and exposes a cancellation token. 5) Compatibility Layer: translator module that maps legacy function-calling shapes into the structured wrapper and preserves legacy fields under a legacy.* namespace.

Key heuristics: - Depth limit default=8 (config per-tenant) with soft limit at 6 where we attempt summarization by invoking the summarize tool before further calls. - Cycle detection sensitivity: detect >=3 repeated signatures within a single request window -> halt. - Time budget: per-request tool time budget (default 6s per tool, aggregate 30s) where exceeding triggers best-effort summarize-and-halt. - If a tool result is truncated, set truncated=true and attach truncated_reason: "token_limit" or "timeout".
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Design + API contract spec for structured result wrapper and streaming boundary events (docs + proto) — owner: Liam
Phase 2: Implement Invocation Guard and Reentrancy Detector in runtime core, unit tests, local fakes — owner: Nadia
Phase 3: Safe Injector + sanitizers; integrate with KMS policies and code-exec safe-list — owner: Rohit
Phase 4: Streaming Adapter changes for SDKs (Node/Python) and server streaming protocol updates — owner: SDK team
Phase 5: Compatibility Layer: implement translator for legacy function shapes and a migration-mode flag — owner: Integration Engineers
Phase 6: End-to-end integration tests + load tests (simulate 100k chained requests to validate performance impact) — owner: SRE
Phase 7: Gradual rollout behind feature flag, shadowing on 10% traffic, monitor telemetry and customer-facing errors, then widen to 100% — owner: Product + Release
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Spike complete for reentrancy detector prototypes. Two approaches evaluated: (A) call-signature LRU + counts; (B) constraint-solver with graph traversal. Chose approach A for performance and predictability.
2026-03-04: API contract PR (w/ examples) opened in docs repo: structured wrapper and streaming markers. Requesting design review from APIs and SDKs.
2026-03-06: Implemented initial Invocation Guard + per-request context propagation. Added request id tagging for all tool calls. Basic unit tests added.
2026-03-09: Safety sanitizer prototype added for code-exec tool: rejects results containing 'rm -rf' style patterns and long uninterpretable token repeats. Needs security review for false positives.
review_feedback: PM (Mar 03): Prefer soft-fail summarization before halting for PLG users — helps avoid breaking demos. Keep hard halts for enterprise tenants with strict SLOs.
Design (Mar 05): Suggest clearer UX messages for streaming cancellations: include human-friendly reason + structured code to allow clients to detect and recover.
Security (Mar 08): Sanitize list looks good but needs approval from Threat Modeling. Add explicit allowlist/denylist config per tool type and ensure HSM/KMS ops audited.
SRE (Mar 09): Concern about the reentrancy LRU memory growth on long-lived requests. Suggest capped size by tokens and eviction by time-first rather than strict-count.
testing_plan: Unit tests for Invocation Guard lifecycle and context propagation
Fuzz harness that randomly composes tool chains (up to 20 tools) to validate halting heuristics and measure false positives
Integration tests: legacy function-calling payloads -> compatibility translator -> structured wrapper mapping assertions
End-to-end system test that asserts streaming boundary events are emitted and cancellation produces deterministic runtime state
Load test: simulated 100k concurrent requests with normal and adversarial chain patterns to quantify latency tail impact
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged rollout: off by default. Enable shadow mode on 5% of traffic for 48h, collect errors and telemetry but do not alter runtime behavior.
Enable active mode on 10% of low-risk traffic with soft limits only (summarize instead of hard halt). Monitor customer errors for 72h.
Enable hard halts for enterprise tenants behind dedicated config after opt-in. Gradually increase to 100% after two weeks and zero critical incidents.
Provide migration guide for integrators using legacy function payloads and a compatibility toggle in the Console.
